artifacts.summary: 4-phase plan: delete the flaky wall-clock assertion from the injected subprocess source, then extend the timing-marker AST guard to see clock-read/bound-assert pairs inside embedded source strings, with RED self-tests and a single parallel gate run.

memory_candidates.content: AST-based CI guards that scan test bodies for a pattern (e.g. clock-read + bound-assert) have a structural blind spot at string-literal boundaries: code handed to subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-c', src]) or exec/eval is a single ast.Constant to the outer scan, so the pattern is invisible. Closing it needs three steps, not one: (1) recognize subprocess/exec-style call targets, (2) resolve simple same-scope local string bindings (the string is usually bound to a name first and referenced inside a list literal, not passed inline), (3) ast.parse the resolved string under try/except SyntaxError and re-apply the EXISTING detectors against the sub-tree, unioning results with the function's own nodes. Two traps: a tmp_path fixture breaks any label computation built on path.relative_to(REPO_ROOT), and a guard module that duplicates its detection logic inline in a second self-test will silently drift unless both call sites are routed through the shared helpers.
